# AI Prompt Log: Project 2 (Yelp New Orleans)

## How I used AI
I used Claude throughout this project. It drafted most of the R code I ran
(the chunked review import, the spatial joins, the reviewer normalization, the
plots) and drafted text for the report and README. I ran every step myself,
checked the output against my data, made the choices about the category theme,
the geographic system, and the cutoffs (with its recommendations), and edited
the text. The entries below are the exchanges where I tested its work or it
had to change.

## 1. Reading the 5.3 GB review file
**Asked:** How to load the review file, since the assignment's plain
`stream_in()` call might exhaust memory.
**AI gave:** A chunked version that keeps only reviews for my 2,259
restaurants, and a test on the first 100,000 lines first.
**What I did:** Ran the test (8,358 matches, expected columns), then the full
run (6,990,280 records scanned, 476,421 kept). Checked that every kept review
belongs to one of my restaurants, that no columns had missing values, and that
the saved file read back with the same row count.

## 2. File size: the AI corrected itself
**Asked:** Reported the saved review file size (112 MB), then shared a
screenshot of my Console.
**AI gave:** First said 112 MB was the `xz` size. My screenshot showed I had
saved with `xz` and then overwritten the same file with `gzip`, so it
corrected itself: 112 MB was the gzip size.
**What I did:** Kept the full file out of Git (over GitHub's 100 MB limit) and
committed a version without the review text (7.9 MB, same 476,421 reviews).

## 3. Category group
**Asked:** Which related categories to use, after pasting the top 40 counts.
**AI gave:** Candidate themes, a warning that generic labels like "food" and
"bars" are too broad, and a search for related labels I might have missed.
**What I did:** Chose seafood and Louisiana cooking. The search found "seafood
markets" and "fish & chips"; I checked they would add only 3 new restaurants
and left them out. Ran pair counts (cajun/creole with seafood: 156 restaurants)
and the distribution of how many of the four categories each restaurant has.

## 4. The AI's wrong guess about ZIP 70130
**Asked:** For help writing up my choice of ZIP code areas.
**AI gave:** Before writing, it said its earlier description of 70130 as "large"
and "the French Quarter" might be wrong, and searched. The sources conflicted
and several were clearly unreliable. The credible ones put 70130 at about 2.6
square miles, so it is small and dense.
**What I did:** Changed the argument from "ZIP too large" to "one small ZIP
holds 32% of the restaurants," and did not name neighborhoods in the report
because I could not verify them.

## 5. The ranking cutoff changed after I tested it
**Asked:** What minimum number of reviews to require before ranking.
**AI gave:** First suggested 20. I ran a sensitivity check: the top 10 at a
minimum of 5 shared 0 restaurants with the one at 20, and 7 with the one at 30.
At 5, every top-10 restaurant had only 6 to 16 eligible reviews. The AI
revised its recommendation to 30.
**What I did:** Used 30 (345 of 656 restaurants) and report that the top 10
depends on the cutoff.

## 6. Explaining rank changes: the first explanation was incomplete
**Asked:** Why some restaurants move more than 100 places after adjustment.
**AI gave:** An explanation based on reviewer baselines (generous versus tough
reviewers). When I printed the baseline and the gap between eligible and all
reviewers for four of the movers, the baselines were about the same (3.86 to
4.02), and the gap was the driver, so the text was rewritten. I also found
Ruby Slipper Cafe was listed twice because it has two locations.
**What I did:** Rewrote that paragraph. (Add: what you found for the other six.)

## 7. A render failure caused by the AI's code
**Asked:** Pasted "Execution halted" and the error.
**AI gave:** The error came from code it wrote: joining two tables that both
had `business_name` renamed the column, so a later `select()` failed. The
earlier render had also failed, which is why Step 7 was missing from the
report on GitHub.
**What I did:** Applied the fix, rendered again, checked that Step 7 and all
four figures were present, and viewed the page on GitHub.

## 8. Date parsing
**Asked:** Pasted a warning that `ymd(date)` failed and a count showing all
249,002 dates were NA.
**AI gave:** A request to look at the column first. It held text like
"2017-01-14 20:54:15", so `ymd_hms()` was needed. (Dates are not used in the
final ratings analysis.)

## Where the AI was wrong
- It said 112 MB was an `xz` file size; it was the gzip size.
- It guessed ZIP 70130 was the French Quarter and large; it is small and dense.
- It first recommended a 20-review cutoff, before the sensitivity check.
- Its first explanation of the rank movers used only reviewer baselines.
- Its top-10 table code had a column-name clash that broke the render.
